question: Yellow bag in BMW (Biomedical Waste) Rules 2016 is for:
options: B. Infectious waste, anatomical waste, soiled waste
explanation:
• Yellow: human anatomical, soiled (dressings, bedding), infectious.
• Red: recyclable contaminated; White/translucent: sharps.

question: Chlorination of water is done to:
explanation:
• Chlorine kills bacteria, viruses; residual chlorine maintains safety in distribution.
• Breakpoint chlorination removes odor and ensures disinfection.

question: Vector of malaria is:
explanation:
• Female Anopheles transmits Plasmodium (malaria).
• Aedes: dengue, chikungunya; Culex: filariasis.

question: MPN in water quality testing stands for:
explanation:
• MPN: Most Probable Number—estimates coliform bacteria in water sample.
• Indicates fecal contamination.

question: Safe disposal of sharps (needles) should be in:
explanation:
• Sharps must go in puncture-proof, leak-proof containers (white/translucent as per BMW).
• Prevents needlestick injuries.

question: Dengue is transmitted by:
explanation:
• Aedes aegypti (day-biting) transmits dengue virus.
• Also transmits chikungunya, Zika.

question: Occupational health hazard in healthcare includes:
options: B. Needlestick injuries, infections, chemical exposure, stress
explanation:
• Healthcare workers: needlestick, blood-borne infections, chemicals, radiation, musculoskeletal injury, stress.
• PPE and protocols reduce risk.

question: Boiling of water for how long is considered safe for drinking?
explanation:
• Rolling boil for 5-10 minutes (or 1 min at altitude) kills most pathogens.
• Simple method for household water safety.

question: Blue bag in BMW (as per some guidelines) may be used for:
options: B. Glass and metallic body waste (after disinfection)
explanation:
• Color coding may vary; blue can be for glass/metallic waste (broken glass, etc.) after disinfection.
• Follow local BMW rules.

question: Prevention of mosquito breeding includes:
options: A. Storing water in open containers
B. Removing stagnant water, covering containers, use of larvicides
explanation:
• Eliminate stagnant water, cover containers, use mosquito nets, larvicides where needed.
• Source reduction is key for dengue and malaria control.

question: Chlorine demand in water is:
options: A. Amount of chlorine consumed before residual is left
explanation:
• Chlorine demand = chlorine used to oxidize organics and kill organisms before residual remains.
• Residual chlorine indicates safe water.

question: Black bag in BMW (general waste) is for:
explanation:
• Black/green (as per BMW 2016): general waste (non-infectious, non-hazardous).
• Segregation at source.

question: Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) vector is:
explanation:
• Sandfly (Phlebotomus) transmits Leishmania (kala-azar).
• Endemic in parts of India (e.g. Bihar).

question: Noise level considered harmful for prolonged exposure (dB):
explanation:
• Prolonged exposure to 85 dB+ can cause hearing loss. Workplace limits apply.
• Normal conversation ~60 dB.

question: Sanitary latrine types include:
options: B. Pit latrine, pour-flush, septic tank
explanation:
• Sanitary options: pit latrine, pour-flush, septic tank, sewerage.
• Swachh Bharat: toilet access and use.

question: Industrial hazard - chemical exposure: nurse should:
options: B. Use PPE, follow MSDS, decontaminate as protocol
explanation:
• PPE, Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS), decontamination, reporting.
• Occupational health nursing.

question: Waterborne disease includes:
explanation:
• Waterborne: cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A, diarrhea (many).
• Vector-borne: malaria, dengue.

question: Incineration is used for:
options: B. High-temperature burning of infectious/hazardous waste
explanation:
• Incineration: burning at high temp to destroy infectious waste. Emissions controlled.
• Alternative: autoclave, shredding for some waste.

question: Air pollution indicator gas that is harmful:
options: B. CO, SO2, NO2, particulate matter
explanation:
• Air pollutants: CO, SO2, NO2, PM2.5, PM10, ozone. Affect respiratory health.
• AQI used for reporting.

question: Double pit latrine advantage:
options: B. One pit used while other decomposes; alternating use
explanation:
• Two pits: use one while other contents decompose. Reduces emptying need.
• Sanitation in rural areas.

question: Radiation safety in healthcare:
options: B. Time, distance, shielding; minimize exposure
explanation:
• Radiation protection: minimize time, maximize distance, use shielding (lead apron).
• ALARA principle.

question: Waste segregation at source means:
options: B. Separating waste by type (infectious, sharp, general) at point of generation
explanation:
• Segregation at source: separate at point of generation (color-coded bins).
• Ensures proper disposal and reduces risk.

question: Culex mosquito transmits:
explanation:
• Culex: filariasis, Japanese encephalitis. Anopheles: malaria. Aedes: dengue, chikungunya.
• Vector identification for control.

question: Residual chlorine in drinking water (mg/L) should be:
explanation:
• Residual chlorine 0.2-0.5 mg/L (or per BIS/local standard) ensures safety in distribution.
• Too high: taste/odor.

question: Occupational health nursing includes:
options: B. Surveillance, health education, first aid, referral, workplace assessment
explanation:
• OH nursing: health surveillance, education, first aid, ergonomics, referral.
• Protect worker health.
